questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Trigonometric Equation Involving Sine with Quadrantal Angles
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{sin}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2 & =0 \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =2 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(1)={90}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${90}^{∘}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={90}^{∘}.$ 

As this is a quadrantal angle, to find the remaining solutions we use our knowledge of the sine function. We know that the sine function has its maximum values at:

$$
x={90}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n
$$

Since the domain $-{180}^{∘}<x\le {180}^{∘}$ is one period, and we have already found one maximum value in this period, we conclude that $x={90}^{∘}$ is the only solution.

questions.problem: Calculate, in degrees, rounded to the nearest integer, the solutions to the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\frac{2}{3}$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\frac{2}{3})=41.810{…}^{∘}≈{41.81}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${41.81}^{∘}$ lies inside the range, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={41.81}^{∘}.$

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={41.81}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the second quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={41.81}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13977985/assets/bc0c031fe6ccbb40dc77474582b301456f537ee2a649ba2d5b3bca9b1240618f.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $2$nd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={180}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}-{41.81}^{∘} \\  & ={138.19}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions (rounded to the nearest integer) are $x={42}^{∘},{138}^{∘}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Trigonometric Equation Involving Sine with Quadrantal Angles
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{sin}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =0 \\ \sqrt{3} & =\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ 1 & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(1)={90}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${90}^{∘}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={90}^{∘}.$ 

As this is a quadrantal angle, to find the remaining solutions we use our knowledge of the sine function. We know that the sine function has its maximum values at:

$$
x={90}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n
$$

Since the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}$ is one period, and we have already found one maximum value in this period, we conclude that $x={90}^{∘}$ is the only solution.

questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-0.7)=-44.427\,004{…}^{∘}≈-{44.4270}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $x=-{44.4270}^{∘}$ is not in the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ To get the first solution that's within the required domain, we need to find an angle that's coterminal with $-{44.4270}^{∘}.$ To do this, we simply add ${360}^{∘}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-{44.4270}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}={315.5730}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Our first solution lies in the fourth quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={44.4270}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={44.4270}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13977985/assets/f3d2d41e1a58dd562ed47ae7e5fcdc79382c426700f520a1153111bfcf2d734b.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={180}^{∘}+{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}+{44.4270}^{∘} \\  & ={224.4270}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions are 

$$
x≈{224.4}^{∘},\,x≈{315.6}^{∘}.
$$

questions.problem:
Expressed in **ascending order** in degrees, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions to the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-0.6,$ for $-{180}^{∘}<x\le {180}^{∘},$ are

$x≈$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$, $\,x≈$
{{field-2}}${}^{∘}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-0.6)=-36.869\,897…≈-36.8699
$$

Since $-{36.8699}^{∘}$ lies inside the given domain, our first solution is

$$
{x}_{1}=-{36.8699}^{∘}.
$$

Our first solution lies in the fourth quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={36.8699}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={36.8699}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13977985/assets/8d88b4ccfe08c26c9d56effaf651e04703995ffaec4b7ab08187f62ddd1897de.png)

A second solution $X$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, and we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={180}^{∘}+{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}+{36.8699}^{∘} \\  & ={216.8699}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

However, this value is not in the required domain. To get the second solution ${x}_{2}$ that's within the given domain, we subtract ${360}^{∘}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}=X-{360}^{∘} & ={216.8699}^{∘}-{360}^{∘} \\  & =-{143.1301}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions are 

$$
x≈-{143.1}^{∘},\,x≈-{36.9}^{∘}.
$$
